assessments.reasoning: I reopened the retained original README at the enrolled Go project mirror revision. The full-body digest and both span digests matched. The opening identifies Go by name and describes it as a programming language developed as open source. This supports the statement and the kind and name fields. The installation span only clarifies that the project also distributes software. The claim explicitly assigns active to the Language Index, so it makes no assertion about project activity, toolchain maintenance, or release support. The protected index record documents an active decision for the exact subject at the protected revision. Taken together, the records justify retaining that tuple in that index snapshot. The evidence-binding gap is that revision 1 cites only the README and scopes its authority only to the Go authors. Its limitation explains what active means but does not bind the index decision that supplies its value.

challenge.method: Hold the README, entity ID, kind, and name fixed and test whether the adopted rules would allow the index to retire the entity. Then compare the actual protected decision with the claim and trace the authority for each field.
challenge.results: Retirement can preserve the same ID and external identity facts. The validator checks allowed states and exact agreement with the claim. It supplies no rule deriving active from those facts. The protected record affirmatively records active and points back to this same claim, so it establishes the index's decision only. The smallest correction is an explicit binding to that protected decision at its exact revision for the state field, with the index identified as its authority. The README binding remains sufficient for the external identity facts. Until the local binding is recorded, the whole-value finding remains insufficient.

limitations: Active is the Language Index classification of the Go language identity.
The identity is scoped to the Go project governed by the recorded publisher and does not classify any toolchain, distribution, or release support status.
Language Index active classification belongs to the index. The README does not establish support status for a compiler or any release.
